evidence.summary: Exhaustive sweep of all 63,488 finite FP16 values: 5,606 inputs exceed the 1e-6 absolute tolerance; max error 5.03e-6 at x=0.622. Violations concentrate in the rational-approximation region.

rationale: The polynomial constants appear truncated to ~4-5 significant digits compared to Cephes double values, so the rational approximation error is plausibly around 1e-5 or larger — well above the 1e-6 absolute tolerance the contract demands for every legal input.

scope_evidence.summary: Every output element must satisfy abs(actual[i] - atan(x[i])) <= 1e-6, and every finite FP16 value is legal, so accuracy must hold over the entire FP16 domain.

scope_rationale: The contract requires abs(actual - atan(x)) <= 1e-6 for every finite FP16 input; testing all finite FP16 values (≤131072 elements) directly covers the declared domain.
statement: The FP32 Cephes-style approximation with truncated coefficients fails the 1e-6 absolute tolerance for some finite FP16 inputs.

evidence.summary: Signed zeros, subnormals, and ±65504 all produce outputs within 5.2e-8 of FP64 atan — far inside the 1e-6 tolerance.

rationale: The kernel uses magnitude, tl.where(x<0,-value,value), and guards reciprocal with maximum(magnitude,1.0) only in the upper branch; need runtime evidence that zeros, subnormals and extrema are handled correctly within tolerance.

scope_evidence.summary: Signed zeros, subnormals and ±65504 are explicitly legal; output must be fresh finite FP32 with abs error <= 1e-6.

scope_rationale: Contract explicitly includes signed zeros, subnormals, and ±65504 in the legal domain with the same 1e-6 bound.
statement: Edge inputs (signed zeros, subnormals, ±65504) produce correct outputs within tolerance.
